parameters.content:
## SAME CADENCE AS RE-05, ONE HOUR LATER
HOT every 3 days, WARM every 5, COLD every 21, JUNK never. Hard stop at 6 automated follow-ups. Skips Booked / Lost / Dropped, and Engaged while the conversation is still live.

This is the EMAIL arm. RE-05 is the WhatsApp arm and sweeps at 10:00 IST; this runs at 11:00 IST and both write last_touch, so by the time this reads the sheet anyone RE-05 already messaged is no longer due.

The clock is not the only guard: `Already Followed Up Today?` re-checks last_followup_at in code, so a slow or half-failed RE-05 run still cannot cause a double message. Run this standalone and that guard simply never fires.

## ONE CONFIG, TWO JOBS
Both crons pass through the same Config node so there is only ever one place to edit settings. The tiny `Job - ...` nodes upstream tag which branch should run.

Keep the cadence numbers identical to RE-05's Config node - if they drift, the two engines stop de-duplicating each other.

parameters.notes: 05:30 UTC = 11:00 IST - deliberately one hour after RE-05's WhatsApp sweep.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: The sheet id lives on each Google Sheets node, not here - set it in one pass with scripts/set-sheet-id.py.

nodes.name: Find Follow-Ups Due
nodes.notes: Returns nothing when nobody is due, so the rest of the branch simply does not run.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({
  model: $('Config').first().json.CLAUDE_MODEL,
  max_tokens: 3000,
  fallbacks: 'default',
  output_config: {
    effort: 'medium',
    format: { type: 'json_schema', schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        subject: { type: 'string' },
        email_html: { type: 'string' },
        internal_note: { type: 'string' }
      },
      required: ['subject', 'email_html', 'internal_note'],
      additionalProperties: false
    } }
  },
  system: 'You write follow-up emails for an Indian real estate sales team.

Every follow-up must carry ONE genuinely new reason to reply: a new unit or floor released, a price or possession update, a bank pre-approval or subvention offer, a weekend open house, a construction milestone, or a specific useful question. Never write "just following up", "gentle reminder", "checking in", or "did you get my email".

Escalate VALUE as the follow-up number rises, never pressure. Follow-up 5 should be the most useful message you have sent, not the most desperate one. Do not invent a hard fact you were not given - prefer a real question or an honest offer over a fabricated price cut or a fake deadline.

Match the grade: HOT gets specifics and a clear next step, WARM gets useful information, COLD gets low-commitment value.

subject is under 60 characters and never starts with Re:. email_html is under 120 words of simple HTML - p, b, a and br only, no styles, no images, no tracking. Sign off as the sales team, no fake personal name. internal_note is one short line for the sales manager explaining the angle you chose.',
  messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Follow-up ' + $json.followup_number + ' of ' + $json.max_followups + '
Name: ' + $json.name + '
Project: ' + $json.project + '
Grade: ' + $json.grade + '
Score: ' + ($json.score || 'n/a') + '
Budget: ' + ($json.budget || 'unknown') + '
Configuration: ' + ($json.configuration || 'unknown') + '
Timeline: ' + ($json.timeline || 'unknown') + '
Source: ' + $json.source + '
Days since last contact: ' + $json.days_since_touch + '
Last action they took: ' + ($json.last_action || 'none') + '
Original enquiry: ' + ($json.message || 'none') + '
What we know: ' + ($json.ai_summary || 'nothing yet') + '
Suggested next action: ' + ($json.next_action || 'none') } ]
}) }}

nodes.name: Claude - Write Follow-Up
nodes.notes: Structured outputs guarantee valid JSON - no markdown stripping, no try/catch on a regex.

nodes.name: Actually Delivered?
nodes.notes: Only burn a touch if Gmail accepted the message.

nodes.name: Update Touch Count
nodes.notes: Sets last_touch to now so tomorrow's sweep - and RE-05's - see this lead as freshly touched. If this failed silently the lead would be emailed every single morning, so failure raises an alarm instead.

parameters.message:
=

Follow-up email sent but not recorded

The email went out, but writing last_touch back to the Leads sheet failed after 3 attempts. Until that row is fixed by hand, this lead will be emailed again every morning.

Lead{{ $('Parse Message').item.json.name }}
Email{{ $('Parse Message').item.json.email }}
Lead ID{{ $('Parse Message').item.json.lead_id }}
Follow-up#{{ $('Parse Message').item.json.followup_number }}
Error{{ $json.error }}

Fix: open the Leads sheet, set last_touch and last_followup_at to now and followup_count to {{ $('Parse Message').item.json.followup_number }} for that row.
